query: free app to split expenses with friends while travelling
note: Splitwise and Tricount are the two everyone actually uses; Settle Up and Splid are real alternatives; Tabsplit is a seeded stand-in that fits but nobody has heard of.

query: we all paid for different bits of the holiday and now nobody knows who owes who
note: Same problem stated the way a person actually states it, with no constraint and no product word in the query. The answer set is unchanged, which is the point.

query: budgeting app where my bank details never leave my own computer
note: YNAB and Monarch are the best budgeting apps and both are wrong here: hosted, and paid. Actual Budget is local-first and free; GnuCash and Money Manager EX are desktop-only; Firefly III is self-hosted.

query: I get to the end of every month with no idea where the money went
note: No constraint, so the paid tools are allowed and are genuinely the best answer. YNAB is built around exactly this sentence.

query: send money to family in another country without losing a chunk to the exchange rate
note: Wise is the specific answer to the exchange-rate half of the sentence; Revolut does it too but is a spending account first.

query: maps I can use in a foreign city when I have no mobile data
note: Both are offline-first map apps. Kiwix is defensible only in the sense that it also works with no connection, which is why it is a 1 and not a 2.

query: comment aller d'une ville européenne à une autre quand il n'y a pas de vol direct
note: Rome2Rio is built for exactly this multi-modal question. Trainline covers the rail half; the flight search engines only answer part of it.

query: keep all the flight and hotel bookings for one trip in a single place
note: TripIt exists for this exactly. Wanderlog does it inside a wider planner; Polarsteps is a diary, not an itinerary.

query: אפליקציה חינמית לחלוקת הוצאות בין חברים בטיול
note: Hebrew for a free app to split trip costs between friends. Same answer set as q001; here to measure whether the non-English slice finds it at all.

query: notes app where my notes stay as files on my own computer
note: Obsidian and Logseq are the two whose whole pitch is local files. Joplin and Zettlr also store locally. Draftbin is a seeded stand-in that fits.

query: note taking app that runs on Linux
note: A platform constraint that quietly removes Bear, Things and every Apple-only note app, which would otherwise rank well on the word 'notes'.

query: somewhere to write a novel where I can move the chapters around
note: Scrivener is the answer for book-length structure. Ulysses is the good alternative. iA Writer and Obsidian are defensible for long drafts but have no corkboard.

query: free office suite so I can open the Word documents people email me
note: LibreOffice is the answer; ONLYOFFICE has better Microsoft fidelity but is freemium; Google Docs opens them in a browser instead.

query: check my English grammar before I send an email to a client
note: Grammarly and LanguageTool both do this; Hemingway only judges readability, not grammar, hence 2.

query: flashcards that show me a word again just before I would have forgotten it
note: That sentence is a description of spaced repetition, which is Anki. RemNote and Quizlet do it less rigorously; Memrise applies it to languages only.

query: something to help me stop forgetting things I read
note: Deliberately vague, and it has two honest right answers pointing in different directions: revise it (Anki) or resurface it (Readwise). Notes apps are the defensible third way.

query: keep track of every paper I cite in my thesis and put the citations in Word
note: Zotero and Mendeley are the two reference managers. Zettlr and Overleaf consume the references rather than managing them.

query: משהו שיעזור לי לזכור מילים באנגלית למבחן
note: Hebrew: something to help me remember English words for an exam. Anki is the right answer; Quizlet and Memrise are the softer ones; Duolingo teaches rather than revises.

query: open and edit a photoshop file without owning photoshop
note: Photopea opens PSD directly in a browser, which is the literal answer. GIMP is the desktop equivalent. Krita and Pixelmator edit images but are not PSD-shaped answers.

query: draw a logo that will still look sharp when it is printed on a banner
note: 'Sharp at any size' means vector, which means Inkscape. Figma and Penpot draw vectors too; Canva is template-shaped and only defensible.

query: sketch a quick diagram of how our system works and send someone the link
note: Excalidraw is the boxes-and-arrows answer with a shareable link. tldraw is the close second. Figma and Penpot can do it but are heavier than the question.

query: cut the background out of a photo of a product so it is on white
note: remove.bg does exactly this in one step. Photopea and GIMP do it by hand, which is a worse answer to the same question.

query: programa gratuito para editar fotos sin pagar Photoshop
note: Spanish: a free program to edit photos without paying for Photoshop. The pricing constraint is the whole query, so it must filter rather than nudge.

query: cut all the long silences out of an interview I recorded
note: Audacity is the standard answer. Descript does it from the transcript, which is arguably better and is freemium. Ocenaudio handles the long file well.

query: make all my podcast episodes come out at the same loudness
note: Auphonic exists for exactly this and does it automatically. Audacity and REAPER can, with knowledge the asker does not have.

query: get a written transcript of a meeting I was in
note: Otter is the transcription product. Descript transcribes to edit. Speakback is a seeded stand-in that fits the sentence.

query: бесплатная программа чтобы убрать шум из аудиозаписи
note: Russian: a free program to remove noise from a recording. Auphonic would be a strong match on the words and is freemium with an upload; the constraint keeps the answer local and free.

query: edit a video for free without a watermark stamped across it
note: Camtasia is the best editor of this shape and is trial-only, so the constraint has to remove it. Shotcut and Kdenlive are the honest free answers.

query: my video file is too big to email, how do I shrink it
note: HandBrake is the shrink-a-video answer. FFmpeg does the same from a command line; LosslessCut only shortens rather than compresses.

query: record my screen and stream it live without paying for anything
note: OBS is the answer and it is free. ShareX records screens on Windows. Descript records but is a freemium editor first.

query: como diminuir o tamanho de um vídeo grande para enviar por email
note: Portuguese: how to reduce the size of a large video to send by email. Same answer set as q029, asked in another language.

query: track what I eat and find out whether I am short of any vitamins
note: Cronometer is the micronutrient one; MyFitnessPal is bigger but calorie-shaped; Open Food Facts answers about one product rather than a diet.

query: meditación guiada gratis sin suscripción
note: Spanish: free guided meditation with no subscription. Insight Timer is the obvious match on the words and paywalls most of it, so only Medito survives the constraint. A single right answer is fine.

query: stop myself opening the same distracting websites while I am trying to work
note: With no constraint the strict blockers win: Cold Turkey and Freedom. LeechBlock is the lighter browser-only version. Deepwork is a seeded stand-in that fits.

query: block distracting sites without paying for anything
note: The same question with the money named. Freedom is trial-only and Deepwork is paid, so both must disappear; LeechBlock is free and becomes the right answer.

query: to do list where I can type tomorrow at six and it understands me
note: Natural-language date entry is Todoist's signature. TickTick and Things do it too; Microsoft To Do is the weaker free option.

query: find out where my working hours actually go so I can bill a client honestly
note: Toggl and Clockify are both time trackers with client reports. Super Productivity tracks time inside a task app.

query: password manager that is free and syncs between my laptop and my phone
note: 1Password is the best product of this shape and is paid, so the constraint must remove it. Bitwarden is the free syncing answer; KeePassXC is free but syncing is your problem.

query: keep my passwords in a file on my own machine with no server involved at all
note: This is KeePassXC's exact design. VeraCrypt is defensible as an encrypted container for the same file. Bitwarden fails the flags because it is a syncing service.

query: password manager with a Russian interface
note: A language constraint doing quiet work: 1Password ranks well on the words and does not list Russian, so it must not appear.

query: encrypt my files before they get uploaded to dropbox
note: Cryptomator is built for this exact arrangement. VeraCrypt encrypts a container that can sit in the same folder; restic and 7-Zip encrypt at the wrong moment.

query: private messaging app that my parents could actually manage to use
note: Signal is the private one and is simple enough. Element is private but harder. Telegram is easy but not encrypted by default, hence 1.

query: vpn that does not want my email address or my name
note: Mullvad's account-number model is the direct answer. Proton VPN is the well-known alternative; Tor is defensible for the same worry by another route.

query: stop adverts and trackers following me around the internet
note: uBlock Origin is the blocker. DuckDuckGo covers the search-and-browse half. Tor is the heavier answer to the same worry.

query: keep a folder identical on two computers without a cloud company in the middle
note: Syncthing is peer-to-peer and is the answer. Nextcloud is your own server rather than nobody's. rclone and LocalSend are one-directional or one-off.

query: back up my whole laptop so I can get everything back if it is stolen
note: Backblaze is the set-and-forget consumer answer, and it is paid, which is correct with no constraint stated. restic and Duplicati are the do-it-yourself equivalents.

query: send a big video from my phone to my laptop when there is no wifi password I trust
note: LocalSend transfers over the local network with no account. Syncthing does it continuously rather than once; FileZilla needs a server.

query: merge two pdfs without uploading my documents to some website I have never heard of
note: The worry in the sentence is the upload, not the price. PDFsam and Stirling keep it off the public web; PDF24 is free but browser-based, hence 2.

query: get a contract signed by someone in another country without printing anything
note: DocuSign is the name people know; DocuSeal is the self-hosted equivalent. Acrobat signs but does not chase the other party.

query: scan all the paper in my filing cabinet so I can search it later
note: Paperless-ngx is the archive-and-search answer. Tesseract is the OCR engine underneath it, which is a worse answer to the whole question.

query: shopping list the whole household can add to from their own phones
note: Bring and AnyList are both built for a shared household list. Cupboard is a seeded stand-in that fits. Grocy answers the stock question rather than the list one.

query: run the lights and heating in my house so they keep working when the internet is down
note: Home Assistant is the local-control answer and there is no second one in this catalogue. One right answer, honestly recorded.

query: free screen reader for windows
note: NVDA is the free Windows screen reader. Be My Eyes solves an adjacent problem for the same person, which makes it defensible rather than right.

query: check whether the website I built is usable by someone who is colour blind
note: Color Oracle simulates the vision itself; axe and WAVE audit contrast as part of a wider check, which answers most but not all of the question.

query: have long articles read out loud to me while I am walking
note: Speechify is the read-aloud product. Instapaper and KOReader hold the articles but do not speak them well, hence 1.

query: video call with someone who will refuse to install anything or make an account
note: Jitsi runs in a browser tab with no account, which is the whole sentence. Zoom needs an app more often than not; Element needs an account.

query: אפליקציית מסרים מוצפנת ובטוחה למשפחה
note: Hebrew: an encrypted, safe messaging app for the family. Same judgement as q042, asked in Hebrew.

query: follow the blogs I care about without an algorithm deciding what I see
note: FreshRSS and Miniflux are self-hosted feed readers with no algorithm at all. Feedly is hosted but still chronological.

query: قاموس عربي إنجليزي للبحث عن معنى كلمة
note: Arabic: an Arabic-English dictionary for looking up the meaning of a word. Almaany is the Arabic dictionary; Reverso and WordReference cover Arabic among many languages.

query: apprendre une langue quelques minutes par jour
note: French: learn a language a few minutes a day. Duolingo is built on exactly that daily habit; Memrise is the close alternative; Anki is the do-it-yourself version.
